correctness.rationale: Homogeneity gives a bijection between ordered injective types and triangle-free finite extensions over the labelled parameter set. Mixed triangles correspond exactly to horizontal G-edges or vertical F-edges in the Cartesian product, proving the independent-set sum. For any fixed arity r>=2, guessable finite adjacency patterns give #P membership. In the bipartite padding reduction the edgeless labelled tuple graph contributes i(B)^r*2^(rm), while all other contributions after division by 2^(rm) total less than 1/4. Thus a single exact count and a polynomial-time integer rth root recover i(B). The independent-parameter asymptotic uses the exact independent-set counts of a graph with zero, one or at least two edges. From actual verify.py execution, 263 direct checks, 14 specializations and 443 recovery identities passed; all-infinite claims rest on proof, not finite tests.

originality.rationale: The closest public result proves #P-complete finite-parameter counting only for one-variable Henson types and explicitly leaves higher arity untreated. Conant gives general finite-tuple extension consistency, which implies the admissibility criterion and is not claimed as novel; neither that primary paper nor the inspected indexed 1-type result provides fixed-r>=2 #P-completeness on bipartite inputs or the one-query isolated-vertex padding reduction. Henson supplies the classical homogeneity theorem; Provan-Ball supplies the hard independent-set source. Originality attaches to the all-fixed-higher-arity metric hardness theorem with its explicit graph-product formula, not to an elementary restatement of homogeneity.
residual_risks: Conant 2014 already gives the general finite-tuple extension feasibility criterion; the Cartesian counting identity is a direct enumeration of that prior criterion, not an independent novelty claim.
A specialized paper or unindexed result may contain an equivalent fixed-higher-arity counting-complexity reduction under other language.
Full Provan-Ball source text was not inspected; its quoted #P-completeness fact is established in the publisher abstract and in later literature.

value.rationale: The natural finite-parameter orbit count for injective multi-types is put into exact graph-product form for all fixed arities, with a one-query #P-completeness theorem even under bipartite input restriction. This fills the arity>=2 gap left by the closest existing 1-type counting result and reveals a precise two-leading-term independent-parameter type spectrum; it is not a mere alteration of a parameter in an already quantified theorem. The exact hardness of this natural invariant can inform model-theoretic type enumeration and algorithm design; no unproved downstream theorem is claimed.
